Collecting geo-point data with terroir

Source: vignettes/terroir.Rmd
terroir.Rmd
library(terroir)

Why

A grower or agronomist assembling covariates for a trial site asks a plain question: for one exact paddock, can I pull daily temperature and rainfall, a vegetation index, and district farm economics from several public archives, through one interface, and get back a tidy table that carries its own source, licence and retrieval time, without leaking the paddock’s exact coordinates and without a live network connection standing between me and reproducing the analysis next season? This vignette answers with terroir’s own shipped fixtures, offline throughout, and closes on what happens when a source cannot answer at all.

What

terroir pulls climate, weather, vegetation-index, soil, elevation and agricultural-economics data for a single geographic point from many free sources, behind one uniform request-and-response contract. It is the data-collector member of the ORCHESTRA: a producer that feeds covariates and forcings to downstream modelling. Every source is an optional adapter, so terroir installs and works with none of the source packages present.

geo_point_request() builds a request: a point, an optional date range, the variables wanted, and the id of one registered source. list_sources() lists every registered adapter, and register_source() adds one, enforcing the data-collector role’s free-only rule – an adapter that does not reach a free source is refused at registration time, not discovered later as a billing surprise. collect_point() dispatches one request to its adapter and returns a verified geo_point_series, or a structured refusal when the source is unknown, its package is missing, the point falls outside the source’s declared coverage, or a returned value fails a plausibility check. collect_points() runs a whole batch of requests at once and keeps every refusal as an accounted row rather than dropping it from the stack. is_refusal() and is_replayed() tell the two special outcomes apart from an ordinary series; verify_geo_series() and geo_point_schema() are the contract itself, exported so a downstream package can check or type against them directly rather than reaching into terroir’s internals.

Do

The registered sources 

src <- list_sources()
nrow(src)
#> [1] 12
Every source adapter terroir currently registers.
id package free
abares read.abares TRUE
chirps chirps TRUE
elevation geodata TRUE
isric apsimx TRUE
modis MODISTools TRUE
nasapower nasapower TRUE
nert nert TRUE
ocular ocular TRUE
silo weatherOz TRUE
soilgrids geodata TRUE
stac rsi TRUE
worldclim geodata TRUE

Every adapter is free – the data-collector role forbids a paid source, enforced by register_source() itself rather than merely documented.

Registering a new source

The toy adapter below returns a constant value for illustration; a real adapter would call an upstream package instead, the way the built-in sources do.

toy_adapter <- function(request, retrieved_at) {
  dt <- data.table::data.table(
    date = request$start, variable = "toy_index", value = 1
  )
  new_geo_point_series(
    dt, lon = request$lon, lat = request$lat, source = "toy_local",
    source_version = "1.0", license = "CC0", retrieved_at = retrieved_at,
    call = "toy_adapter()"
  )
}
register_source(
  "toy_local", toy_adapter, package = "base", free = TRUE,
  description = "Illustrative in-memory adapter used only in this vignette"
)
"toy_local" %in% list_sources()$id
#> [1] TRUE

The free-only rule is enforced, not merely stated: registering the same adapter under free = FALSE is refused outright, and the refusal names the rule it enforces.

free_only_refusal <- tryCatch(
  register_source("toy_paid", toy_adapter, package = "base", free = FALSE),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
cat(free_only_refusal)
#> Refusing to register "toy_paid": the data-collector role is free-only.
#> ℹ Every adapter must reach a free source (`free = TRUE`).

A request 

req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.6, lat = -34.92,       # Adelaide
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-31",
  variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"),
  source = "nasapower"
)
req
#> <geo_point_request> source "nasapower"
#> point: (138.6, -34.92) range: 2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-31
#> variables: T2M, PRECTOTCORR

Collecting (live)

collect_point() performs the download. It is not run here (this vignette builds offline), but the call is simply:

series <- collect_point(req)
series                 # a geo_point_series: tidy data.table + provenance
attr(series, "provenance")

Offline replay (zero network)

terroir ships a small set of recorded fixtures, one per CORE source. Passing offline = TRUE answers a request from the matching fixture with no network egress at all – useful for a reproducible pipeline, for a continuous-integration run, and (with coarsening, below) for a sovereign coordinate that must never reach an upstream service. A replayed series carries replayed = TRUE in its provenance and keeps the recording’s retrieved_at, so a consumer can always tell a cached series from a live one.

offline_req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.6, lat = -34.92,
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-10",
  variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"),
  source = "nasapower"
)
series <- collect_point(offline_req, offline = TRUE)
is_replayed(series)
#> [1] TRUE
attr(series, "provenance")$retrieved_at   # the fixture's stamp, not now
#> [1] "2026-06-02 00:00:00"
head(series, 3)
#> <geo_point_series> 3 rows from "nasapower" (v4.2.5)
#> variables: "T2M" licence: NASA POWER (free, public)
#>      lon    lat       date variable value   unit    source source_version
#>    <num>  <num>     <Date>   <char> <num> <char>    <char>         <char>
#> 1: 138.6 -34.92 2020-01-01      T2M 20.10   <NA> nasapower          4.2.5
#> 2: 138.6 -34.92 2020-01-02      T2M 23.73   <NA> nasapower          4.2.5
#> 3: 138.6 -34.92 2020-01-03      T2M 29.87   <NA> nasapower          4.2.5
#>           retrieved_at                   license
#>                 <char>                    <char>
#> 1: 2026-06-02 00:00:00 NASA POWER (free, public)
#> 2: 2026-06-02 00:00:00 NASA POWER (free, public)
#> 3: 2026-06-02 00:00:00 NASA POWER (free, public)

Offline mode needs none of the source packages installed: it reads .rds fixtures and never touches an adapter. When no recorded fixture answers a request, offline mode returns a structured refusal rather than silently falling back to the network – the zero-egress guarantee is absolute. A caller can point terroir at their own directory of recorded fixtures with options(terroir.fixture_dir = "/path/to/fixtures"), or switch the whole session offline with options(terroir.offline = TRUE).

A figure: what the replayed series looked like

A geo_point_series is long (one row per date x variable), so plotting it as small multiples – one panel per variable, sharing the date axis – is the natural way to look at what a collector call actually returned.

panel_lab <- c(
  T2M = "air temperature at 2 m (degC)",
  PRECTOTCORR = "total precipitation (mm)"
)
plot_dt <- data.table::copy(series)
plot_dt[, panel := panel_lab[variable]]
ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_dt, ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value, colour = variable)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1L, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "date", y = "daily value") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Adelaide, 1-10 January 2020, replayed from the shipped NASA POWER fixture: daily mean air temperature at 2 m and daily total precipitation. No network call was made to produce this figure.

Sovereign coordinates (coarsening)

A grower’s exact paddock GPS is sensitive. When a point is flagged sovereign = TRUE, terroir coarsens the coordinate to roughly a one-kilometre cell before any upstream call, so the exact location never leaves the host. Both the raw-requested and the coarsened-sent coordinate are recorded in provenance – the host keeps the full record, the upstream service sees only the coarsened point.

sovereign_req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.63124, lat = -34.92871,   # an exact paddock GPS
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-31",
  source = "nasapower",
  sovereign = TRUE                    # coarsening on by default
)
sovereign_req       # prints both the raw and the coarsened (sent) point
#> <geo_point_request> source "nasapower"
#> point: (138.63, -34.93) range: 2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-31
#> variables: (adapter default)
#> coarsened (sovereign): raw (138.63124, -34.92871) -> sent (138.63, -34.93)
#> policy "precision=0.01"

Coarsening is also available for a non-sovereign point via the coarsen argument: a single number rounds to that many degrees of precision (for example coarsen = 0.01 for a roughly 1 km cell), and coarsen = list(grid = 0.25) snaps each coordinate to the nearest quarter-degree grid node. The returned series’ provenance gains sovereign, coarsen_policy, and the raw-vs-sent coordinates; the fixed ten-column series schema is unchanged, so a consumer reading those columns is unaffected.

The response contract 

geo_point_schema()
#>  [1] "lon"            "lat"            "date"           "variable"      
#>  [5] "value"          "unit"           "source"         "source_version"
#>  [9] "retrieved_at"   "license"

Every series carries these ten columns plus a mandatory provenance attribute (source, version, retrieval time, licence, the exact upstream call); verify_geo_series() checks both and fails loudly if either is missing, so a malformed series never flows downstream silently.

verify_geo_series(series)

The unit column is part of the contract but is not yet populated by every adapter: nasapower and abares emit NA_character_ there, and so does nert for actual evapotranspiration, whose unit is ambiguous upstream. The vegetation-index sources set "index", and silo, worldclim, elevation, soilgrids, chirps and the other nert products set a physical unit. verify_geo_series() does not yet warn on an all-NA unit column.

Graceful refusal

If a source’s package is not installed, or its free key is unset, a caller gets a first-class refusal rather than an error.

refused <- suppressWarnings(
  collect_point(geo_point_request(0, 0, source = "not_a_source"))
)
is_refusal(refused)
#> [1] TRUE
refused
#> <terroir_refusal> source "not_a_source"
#> unknown source 'not_a_source' (see list_sources())

Batch collection

collect_points() runs several requests at once and stacks the outcomes into one table, tagged with a request_index and a status column. A refusal contributes exactly one accounted row rather than disappearing from the stack, so a multi-site collection with a dead source still reports every request it was given.

batch_reqs <- list(
  geo_point_request(
    138.6, -34.92, "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10",
    variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"), source = "nasapower"
  ),
  geo_point_request(140.7, -35.30, source = "abares"),
  geo_point_request(0, 0, source = "not_a_source")
)
batch_out <- collect_points(batch_reqs, offline = TRUE)
batch_summary <- batch_out[, .(
  source = source[1L], status = status[1L], n_rows = .N,
  reason = reason[1L]
), by = request_index]
One row per request in a three-request batch (n = 41 stacked rows in total).
request_index source status n_rows reason
1 nasapower ok 20 NA
2 abares ok 20 NA
3 not_a_source refused 1 offline: no recorded fixture answers this request (source ‘not_a_source’, point (0, 0), range NA..NA); offline mode never falls back to the network

Sources at a glance

The registered sources and what each covers.
id upstream domain
nasapower nasapower global climate + solar (no key)
silo weatherOz SILO 5 km grid, Australia (free email key)
abares read.abares Australian gridded farm economics
modis MODISTools MODIS NDVI/EVI
stac rsi Sentinel-2 NDVI via Planetary Computer
nert nert (AAGI-AUS) TERN soil, soil-moisture, AET, canopy height, phenology (Australia; free key)
ocular ocular (AAGI-AUS) Sentinel-2 / Landsat spectral-index series over a 500 m window (Planetary Computer; cloud-masked, no key)
isric apsimx SoilGrids soil profile by depth layer (global, no key)
worldclim geodata WorldClim 2.1 bioclimatic variables bio_1 to bio_19 (global, no key)
elevation geodata SRTM 90 m elevation and slope (non-commercial licence, no key)
soilgrids geodata SoilGrids 2.0 means at 0-60 cm in four depths (CC BY 4.0, no key)
chirps chirps CHIRPS 2.0 daily rainfall, 50 S to 50 N (public domain, no key)

The ocular source takes its index name from variables[1] (default "NDVI") and its sensor from variables[2] ("auto", "sentinel-2", "landsat-8" or "landsat-5"; "auto" by default). Pixel cloud masking is on and cannot be switched off: a date whose window is entirely cloud is dropped from the series rather than returned as a spurious near-zero index.

worldclim, elevation, soilgrids and chirps answer many requests in one upstream call when collect_points() is given a batch, so a set of sites costs one raster read rather than one per site. worldclim and elevation carry non-commercial licences that appear in each series’ provenance. GSODR is enrolled in the ORCHESTRA and lands as an adapter in a future release.

Read

12 sources are currently registered, all free by construction: the free-only rule tested above refuses a paid adapter with an explicit error rather than letting one slip into the registry silently.

Air temperature at Adelaide across the replayed ten days ranges from 15.50 to 31.06 degC – a day-to-day swing typical of Adelaide midsummer once a front moves through – while precipitation is essentially dry: 2 of the ten days record a trace (0.03 and 0.06 mm), and the rest are zero. A collector that returned a flat temperature line or a wet run of days here would be the signal to distrust the fixture before trusting anything built on top of it.

Coarsening moves the sovereign point from its exact (138.63124, -34.92871) to the sent (138.63, -34.93) under the precision=0.01 policy – roughly a one-kilometre cell at this latitude – so only the coarsened point, never the exact paddock GPS, reaches the upstream service.

The three-request batch stacks 41 rows: the two answerable requests (nasapower, abares) each contribute one row per collected value, and the one unregistered source contributes exactly one refused row rather than being dropped, carrying its own reason in the reason column rather than a bare NA.

Limits

The five CORE-source fixtures shipped with this vignette (nasapower, silo, modis, abares, stac) were recorded once, on 2 June 2026: they answer exactly the point, date range and variables recorded in the fixture manifest, and read nothing live, so the temperature and precipitation figures above describe that one recorded January rather than current conditions. nert and ocular ship no offline fixture in this package, so neither their live retrieval nor ocular’s cloud masking is exercised here; NEWS.md documents both in full. silo, abares and nert refuse a point outside Australia’s bounding box, and ocular refuses outside its UTM-defined latitude band, because its window is built in UTM and is undefined further poleward – neither restriction is exercised in this vignette, whose one worked point sits well inside every source’s coverage. Coordinate coarsening rounds to a fixed number of decimal degrees or snaps to a grid; it is not a true geodesic buffer, so the ground distance a coarsened point actually moves varies with latitude rather than being a constant one kilometre everywhere. Several of the external facts this package asserts remain unverified against their own authority – among them the SILO variable codes, the ABARES layer-name dictionary and the Sentinel-2 band mapping – and terroir_external_facts() and terroir_fact_status() enumerate exactly which fact families still need that check before a caller should treat their column semantics as independently confirmed rather than merely upstream-documented.

What to read next

The function reference (?collect_point, ?geo_point_request, ?collect_points) documents every argument in full, including ones this vignette does not exercise, such as passing an explicit retrieved_at for a reproducible live run. terroir_external_facts() and terroir_fact_status() document exactly which external-authority facts this package asserts and which of them have been checked against their own catalogue, family by family. NEWS.md describes the newest source, ocular, and the cloud-masking behaviour this vignette’s offline fixtures do not exercise, in full.

Reproduce

This vignette draws no random numbers: every value comes from the shipped offline fixtures or from the package’s own deterministic code.
